title: Rainfall Totals Map: Any Dates, Any Point
description: Map total rainfall for any dates around any point with the Rainfall Totals Map — ERA5 archive totals for trips, gardens and dry spells. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, published climate averages credit Mawsynram, India with about 11,871 mm (467 inches) of rain a year, while Death Valley manages roughly 60 mm (2.4 inches) — this map lets you pull the actual totals for the dates you care about.
quick_answer: The Rainfall Totals Map sums archived daily precipitation around your point for any start and end dates you choose, using the ERA5 weather archive. Pick a point and a period — last month, a holiday week, a drought year — and read what actually fell, not what usually falls.

A dry spell means little until it is a number against a normal season. Pull both periods onto the same map and the anomaly measures itself.
Averages hide timing: a place can take its rain in three violent weeks or thirty gentle ones. Date-ranged totals across several years show the rhythm, not just the sum.

examples.label: Example · A tale of two averages

body.t: Published averages put Seattle near 952 mm (37.5 in) a year — spread across many grey days — while desert stations a few hundred miles inland record a tenth of that in a handful of storms. Totals alone rank wetness; the date range reveals character.
Each cell sums the archive's daily precipitation over your dates, across a 5×5 grid spanning about 25 miles. A cell is a district's rainfall for your period — not one rain gauge's luck.

faq: Precipitation or rainfall — same thing here?

The archive total is all precipitation water equivalent in the daily sum; this map reads it as rainfall totals for the chosen period. Snow's water content rides inside the number where the model's daily sum includes it.
How far back can I query?
The ERA5 archive reaches back to 1940 in current form. Recent decades rest on far denser observations; mid-century totals carry model-era uncertainty and deserve softer quoting.
Why does the official gauge disagree with my cell?

A gauge is a point; a cell is an area average over roughly 25–30 km of model grid. A storm that parked over the gauge can triple its reading against the cell — both are honest, about different things.
Can I compare this year with the climate normal?
Yes — run the same dates for several years and eyeball the spread, or compare with published 30-year normals for the area. The map gives actuals; the normal is the published expectation.
Does it work for monsoon or Mediterranean climates?
Worldwide — the archive is global. Date-ranged queries are exactly how strongly seasonal climates should be read: wet season and dry season separately, never as one misleading annual blur.
What about snowfall in the total?
Use the Snowfall Totals Map for the frozen archive view; this map's precipitation includes melted-water equivalents in the source data, which is rain-gauge language, not snow-depth language.
Can I use this for a water-rights or insurance claim?
No — claims and rights run on official gauge networks and certified records. This is a research and context tool with honest sourcing, which is a different job.
